title: Misri meets Nepal PM Balendra Shah to prepare his first official visit to India
dek: India's foreign secretary ended two days of talks in Kathmandu. Nepal wants flood-reconstruction aid, a revised trade treaty, new air routes and progress on the boundary dispute.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri called on Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu on Thursday, ending a two-day visit to prepare for Mr Shah's first official trip to India, which officials in both countries expect in the last week of November.

The discussion "focused on the implementation of various bilateral initiatives" and on "possibilities for further enhancement of India-Nepal cooperation" ahead of the "forthcoming high level visit", the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu said, according to one report. Mr Misri conveyed greetings from Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Nepal's foreign ministry said the meeting took place at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, another report said, and that the talks covered the full range of relations, including high-level exchanges, connectivity, trade, development cooperation, energy and people-to-people ties.

## The two days of talks

Besides the prime minister, Mr Misri met Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal, and held delegation-level talks with Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, according to reports. Mr Rai said the visit had been instrumental in laying the groundwork for Mr Shah's trip, which would be his first bilateral foreign visit since taking office, one report said. Mr Shah is also expected to address a business conclave in New Delhi.

On the floods in the Bhote Koshi area, Mr Misri acknowledged "enormous damage and destruction to the infrastructure of Nepal", and said India had already given assistance and would consider further requests for reconstruction, according to one report. Some reports put the likely dates of Mr Shah's visit at 23 to 25 November; neither government has announced them.

## Wednesday

Mr Misri was received at Tribhuvan International Airport by Gehendra Rajbhandari, a joint secretary in Nepal's foreign ministry, and by Sudhakar Dalela, India's newly appointed ambassador to Nepal, according to one report. He also met Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle at the finance ministry in what the minister's secretariat described as a courtesy call. The two discussed "various aspects of economic cooperation between Nepal and India", the secretariat said, according to another report. ## What Nepal wants

Kathmandu wants a substantial Indian assistance package to help rebuild after the 26 August flash floods on the Bhote Koshi river, progress on settling the boundary dispute, a revision of the bilateral trade treaty, and more air entry routes through Indian airspace for international flights, according to a report carried by several outlets. Several joint projects are expected to be inaugurated during Mr Shah's visit.

The floods were among the deadliest in Nepal's recent history. By 30 August, Nepal's disaster authority had put the toll at 768 dead with more than 2,500 people missing, one report said, and Indian nationals were among the missing. India sent relief supplies, search teams and equipment in the days after.

## Background

Mr Shah, who became prime minister in March, leads a government formed by the Rastriya Swatantra Party. India had planned to send Mr Misri to Kathmandu in the second week of May to engage the new government, but that visit was postponed, with protocol issues cited, according to that report. This is Mr Misri's second visit to Kathmandu since he became foreign secretary in July 2024.

The boundary dispute centres on the Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura areas, which Nepal included in a new official map in 2020 and India says are part of its territory.

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

Nepal relies on India for most of its trade, and most of Nepal's overseas cargo moves through the ports of Kolkata and Haldia under the India-Nepal Treaty of Transit, and on to the Raxaul-Birgunj crossing. Nepal also borders Bengal's Darjeeling district, where the Panitanki-Kakarbhitta crossing near Siliguri links the two countries, so decisions on trade and transit reach Bengal's ports and border towns directly.

China has also expanded its infrastructure and investment ties with Nepal in recent years, and a new government's first official visit to New Delhi sets the tone for relations with India. What Mr Shah secures on flood reconstruction, trade and air routes, and how the two sides handle the boundary question, will be watched in Beijing as well as in Delhi.

## What happens next

- Late November: Mr Shah's expected visit to India, possibly 23 to 25 November; dates to be announced.
- Joint projects are expected to be inaugurated during the visit.
